## Question and data

This analysis compares descriptive BMI statistics across income group and
gender. The CSV path is relative to the repository root, which is the Quarto
project execution directory.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

nhanes <- read_csv(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  col_types = cols(
    Marital = col_character(),
    MaritalClean = col_character()
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## Reusable summary

Rows without BMI, income group, or gender are excluded so both implementations
summarize the same complete cases. The function returns the group count, mean,
median, and sample standard deviation of BMI.

```{r}
summarize_bmi <- function(data) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), !is.na(Gender)) |>
    group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
      median_bmi = median(BMI),
      sd_bmi = sd(BMI),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(IncomeGroup, Gender)
}

bmi_summary <- summarize_bmi(nhanes)
bmi_summary |>
  mutate(
    mean_bmi = round(mean_bmi, 2),
    median_bmi = round(median_bmi, 2),
    sd_bmi = round(sd_bmi, 2)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## R and Python parity

The table records the raw and complete-case row counts, number and labels of
groups, and the rounded summaries from both implementations. `TRUE` indicates
the values agree.

```{r}
parity <- read_csv(
  "assignments/assignment04-polyglot/submission/parity-table.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(parity)
```
